facts.t: The British championed municipalities and neglected villages
facts.d: Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution earned him the title father of local self-government in India — but it was directed at municipal boards. Rural sabhas and samitis were left largely untouched, which is why urban local government has a much longer institutional history.

facts.t: Around 14 lakh women hold elected panchayat posts
facts.d: Roughly 49.5% of all elected representatives are women, well above the mandated one-third. The persistent problem is the proxy sarpanch — which is why a Ministry of Panchayati Raj panel has proposed penalties following a 2023 Supreme Court judgment.
The 13th Finance Commission made 85% of local-body grants untied. By the 15th that had fallen to 60%. More money is reaching panchayats than ever, with less freedom over how to spend it.

bank.q: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments came into force in:
bank.e: They were passed in 1992 and came into force in 1993, constitutionalising rural and urban local government respectively.

bank.q: With reference to devolution to panchayats, consider the following statements:
s: Fewer than 20% of states have fully devolved all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects in both law and practice.
District Planning Committees are often non-operational.
Every state has enacted conformity legislation and holds panchayat elections.
bank.e: All three are correct — the gap between formal compliance and real devolution is the central finding.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about panchayat finances?
o: More than 95% of panchayat funds come from central and state grants
Only about 47% of State Finance Commission recommendations are implemented
Centrally sponsored scheme funds are largely untied, maximising autonomy
Untied grants fell from 85% under the 13th Finance Commission to 60% under the 15th
bank.e: CSS funds are tied to specific purposes, which is precisely what reduces panchayat autonomy.

bank.q: Match List I (state initiative) with List II (achievement):
pairs: 2. Panchayat ERP raising own-source revenue by 18%
bank.e: Tamil Nadu's ERP lifted own-source revenue, Odisha ran SFC-led revenue sharing, Kerala pioneered participatory budgeting, and Sikkim achieved full grant utilisation.

bank.as: Panchayats often function as agents of the state rather than as representatives of the people.
bank.rs: They are used chiefly for scheme delivery rather than for governance, with functions overlapping line departments.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Kerala and Karnataka show genuine convergence; several north-eastern and BIMARU states restrict real autonomy.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about panchayat functionaries:
s: Average vacancy in technical staff was around 42% in 2024.
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh were staffed at under 20%.
Infrastructure deficits affect up to 60% of Gram Panchayats.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they explain why proxy leadership persists where training and staffing are weakest.

bank.q: Which state topped the Devolution Index published in February 2025?
bank.e: Karnataka. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were noted for the largest improvements.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed solutions for panchayat governance EXCEPT:
o: A statutory exclusive services list for panchayats
Activity mapping across the three tiers
Merging panchayats into line departments to remove overlap
SDG localisation through Gram Panchayat Development Plans with benchmarks
bank.e: Merging them into line departments would end local self-government altogether. The remedy proposed is clearer demarcation, not absorption.

bank.q: Who proposed a Consolidated Fund for Local Governments?
bank.e: Upendra Baxi — the idea being to give local bodies a constitutionally protected fund rather than leaving them dependent on discretionary transfers.

bank.q: With reference to Gram Sabhas, consider the following statements:
s: Only fifteen states met quorum requirements in more than 75% of villages.
Social audit units on the MGNREGA model are proposed as a remedy.
Audits are routinely followed by corrective action.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Audits without action is listed among the problems — which is why minimum meeting frequency and agenda disclosure are proposed.

bank.q: The Panchayat Advancement Index introduced in 2025 is published by:
bank.e: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, as a multi-domain assessment of panchayat performance.
